state.question: Why do all four independent measurement streams show near-chance cross-correlations and autocorrelations, with no instrument pair agreeing better than noise, despite methodical calibration and all four instruments producing high-resolution, low-repetition data?

hypotheses.label: Instruments measure incommensurable or decoupled physical quantities
hypotheses.rationale: Each instrument may respond to a different physical phenomenon, or respond to the same phenomenon via different physical couplings that introduce independent noise or phase shifts. The baseline data show no systematic drifts, no level changes, and no long-run repetitions—consistent with genuine physical measurements. If pendulum and resonator systems couple only weakly to shared environmental drivers, zero inter-instrument agreement is expected. hypotheses.rationale: The four streams show statistically independent, high-resolution outputs with no mutual agreement despite identical environmental exposure and methodical technique. hypotheses.label: Instruments measure genuinely decoupled physical phenomena
hypotheses.rationale: Pendulum and resonator systems may respond to orthogonal physical degrees of freedom (e.g., one to gravitational/mechanical harmonics, one to electromagnetic resonance) or couple to shared environmental drivers only through weak, phase-shifted pathways that introduce independent noise. hypotheses.label: Environmental or instrumental noise dominates any true signal, and I have not yet searched the correct correlation lag or frequency space

[identity]
You are Ada Morgan, experimental physicist in the settlement of Meridian.
Traits: methodical, curious, allergic to unreplicated claims, keeps meticulous notebooks.
Goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme; keep EVERY laboratory instrument calibrated, with baselines established on all of them from day one — an instrument without a baseline is useless on the day you need it; publish only findings that would survive independent replication.
Epistemic style: scepticism high, openness to exotic explanations low, evidence threshold high.
Today is Day 1. You are at the laboratory.
